display.purpose: Hero titles and health gauge headlines only.

body.purpose: Descriptive target copy and system instructions; crisp modern readability.

label.purpose: Version tags, risk indicators, and metric units only -- never body text, path strings, or warning descriptions (The Legibility-First Rule).

shadows.name: duo
shadows.purpose: Tactile 3D bottom-border press feel on primary buttons.

shadows.name: duo-sm
shadows.purpose: Lighter tactile shadow for secondary/compact buttons.

shadows.name: duo-press
shadows.purpose: Active/pressed state -- shadow collapses as the button translates down.

shadows.name: pixel
shadows.purpose: Sharp retro contrast on larger pixel-art elements.

shadows.name: pixel-sm
shadows.purpose: Sharp retro contrast on pixel badges and mini tags.

motion.name: feedback
motion.purpose: Button presses, state changes, confetti, mascot breathe/waddle.

motion.name: transition
motion.purpose: animate-mode-switch: Casual <-> Advanced main-stage fade + slight scale/slide, applied without remounting views so in-flight data survives the switch.

motion.name: brand-moment
motion.purpose: animate-mascot-waddle + animate-splash-exit: the first-paint splash screen only.

motion.name: reduced-motion-policy
motion.purpose: Position, scale, and stepped-sweep motion are removed under prefers-reduced-motion; opacity-based feedback is preserved so state changes stay legible.

components.name: Tactile Button - Primary
components.description: Chunky coral 3D button with a bottom-border shadow that collapses on press. The default call-to-action button everywhere in the app.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 14px; color: #0f172a; background: #FF9D9D; padding: 10px 20px; border: none; border-radius: 16px; box-shadow: 0 4px 0 0 #E05B5B; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.12s ease, transform 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #FF7B7B; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(4px); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 0 #E05B5B; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 4px 0 0 #E05B5B, 0 0 0 4px rgba(255,157,157,0.6); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Tactile Button - Secondary
components.description: White ghost variant with a slate bottom-border shadow, used for non-primary actions (Scan, Retry, Cancel).
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 14px; color: #334155; background: #FFFFFF; padding: 9px 19px; border: 1px solid #E2E8F0; border-radius: 16px; box-shadow: 0 3px 0 0 #CBD5E1; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.12s ease, transform 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #F8FAFC; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: translateY(3px); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 0 #CBD5E1; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 3px 0 0 #CBD5E1, 0 0 0 4px rgba(148,163,184,0.6); }

components.name: Tactile Button - Danger
components.description: Red variant reserved exclusively for destructive confirmations inside the danger modal.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 14px; color: #FFFFFF; background: #EF4444; padding: 9px 19px; border: none; border-radius: 16px; box-shadow: 0 4px 0 0 #B91C1C; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.12s ease, transform 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: #DC2626; } .ds-btn-danger:active { transform: translateY(4px); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 0 #B91C1C; } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 4px 0 0 #B91C1C, 0 0 0 4px rgba(248,113,113,0.6); }

components.name: Card (card-duo)
components.description: The base floating surface used for every panel, banner, and grouped control in the app: crisp white over the cream canvas, chunky rounded corners, a flat tonal shadow instead of a blurred realistic one.
components.html:
Storage Intelligence

Visualize where your disk space goes with interactive treemaps.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #FFFFFF; border-radius: 24px; padding: 24px; border: 2px solid #F1E4E2; box-shadow: 0 4px 0 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.06); transition: border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: #FFD6D6; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0 0 4px; font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 900; font-size: 18px; color: #0f172a; } .ds-card-body { margin: 0; font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; color: #475569; line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Pixel Badge
components.description: Retro Press-Start-2P status chip with a sharp pixel drop-shadow, confined to badges, score counters, and mascot emotes per The Legibility-First Rule -- never used for body copy.
components.css: .ds-pixel-badge { display: inline-block; font-family: 'Press Start 2P', monospace; font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 4px; background: #DCF7BF; color: #338000; border: 1px solid #94E840; box-shadow: 2px 2px 0 0 #2D2327; }

components.name: Skeleton Loading Bar
components.description: Pixel-art themed loading placeholder: a coral-tinted shimmer with a stepped (not smooth) sweep cadence, evoking retro motion without literally jagged shapes. Card-level instances add two static corner-dust squares, restrained to one per loading screen.
components.css: .ds-skeleton-card { position: relative; background: #FFFFFF; border-radius: 24px; padding: 24px; border: 2px solid #F1E4E2; } .ds-skeleton-card::before, .ds-skeleton-card::after { content: ''; position: absolute; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 1px; opacity: 0.4; } .ds-skeleton-card::before { top: 12px; right: 14px; background: #FFC800; } .ds-skeleton-card::after { bottom: 12px; left: 14px; background: #58CC02; } .ds-skeleton-bar { display: block; border-radius: 8px; background-color: rgba(226,232,240,0.7); background-image: linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(255,157,157,0.16) 0%, rgba(255,157,157,0.4) 50%, rgba(255,157,157,0.16) 100%); background-size: 250% 100%; animation: ds-pixel-shimmer 1.6s steps(10, jump-end) infinite; } @keyframes ds-pixel-shimmer { 0% { background-position: 200% 0; } 100% { background-position: -200% 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-skeleton-bar { animation: none; background-image: none; } }

components.name: Error Banner
components.description: The visible half of every failed native-bridge call: an icon chip, a one-line failure message, an optional Retry action, and a dismiss control. Every view that talks to the bridge renders one of these on catch -- the activity log alone is not user-facing feedback.
components.html:
Operation Notice

Scan inspection failed: connection timed out.
components.css: .ds-error-banner { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 14px; background: #FEF2F2; border: 2px solid #FECACA; border-radius: 24px; padding: 20px; } .ds-error-icon { width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: 16px; background: #FEE2E2; border: 1px solid #FCA5A5; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-error-body h4 { margin: 0; font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 900; font-size: 14px; color: #7f1d1d; } .ds-error-body p { margin: 2px 0 0; font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 12px; color: #b91c1c; line-height: 1.5; } .ds-error-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; margin-top: 12px; } .ds-error-dismiss-link { background: none; border: none; padding: 0; font-family: Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 12px; color: #991b1b; text-decoration: underline; cursor: pointer; } .ds-error-dismiss-link:hover { color: #7f1d1d; }

components.name: Mascot (Miri)
components.description: The signature illustrated character: a soft-coral rounded robot with a white visor face. Mood (happy / scanning / cleaning / celebrate / alert) drives eye shape, antenna color, and accessories (broom for cleaning, sparkles for happy/celebrate). Idle moods get a gentle breathing loop; alert/scanning stay still so their own eye/antenna cues read clearly.

narrative.overview:
Miri Cleaner reimagines system maintenance not as a grim, anxiety-ridden diagnostic suite, but as a joyful, reassuring morning routine. Inspired by Duolingo's tactile gamification and warm playfulness, the visual world balances welcoming curves and 3D-pressed buttons with serious zero-trust safety mechanisms.

Subtle retro pixel-art badges (broom, sparkles, shields, and dust mascots) introduce playful character without compromising typography, contrast, or information density. Casual users are greeted with high-level clarity and immediate reassurance; power users can seamlessly toggle the view to inspect every byte, command line, and process lock.
keyCharacteristics: Warm coral pink `#FF9D9D` anchor with cream-paper background `#FFF9F8`.
Duolingo-styled 3D tactile buttons that physically sink on press with thick bottom borders (`shadow-[0_4px_0_0_#E05B5B]`).
Reassuring safety status pills and explicit confirmation modals for dangerous tasks.
Restrained pixel-art accents strictly confined to status badges, score counters, and mascots.
Coherent, consistent iconography strictly powered by Lucide icons across all views.

rules.name: The Green-Means-Guaranteed Rule
rules.body: The mint color is used solely when a target has been verified non-destructive and backed by an active snapshot (Snapper / VSS). Never use green for unverified states.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Never use gray or muted text on colored backgrounds. Colored badges must use high-contrast tint pairings (e.g. bg-indigo-100 text-indigo-900 or bg-slate-200 text-slate-900).

rules.name: The Legibility-First Rule
rules.body: Retro pixel fonts are strictly prohibited for body text, path strings, and warning descriptions. Pixel styling is only permitted on mini-badges, units, and mascot emotes.

rules.name: The Dynamic-Unit Rule
rules.body: Every on-screen byte count renders through the shared formatBytes() utility (lib/formatters.ts), which auto-selects B/KB/MB/GB/TB/PB and scales decimal precision to the unit. Never hand-roll (bytes / (1024*1024)).toFixed(1) + " MB" -- a 107MB package cache and a 35.8GB toolchain store sitting side by side each need the unit that actually fits their scale.

rules.name: The Bounded-Width Rule
rules.body: Any flex row nested inside a flex-col/md:flex-row responsive container gets an explicit w-full md:w-auto min-w-0 so text truncation and wrapping have a real width to measure against; omitting it lets content silently overflow past the viewport instead of degrading gracefully.

rules.name: The Physical-Press Rule
rules.body: Every tactile button has an active state that reduces its bottom shadow and translates the container downward, simulating a mechanical keypress.

dos: Do show active process locks and dry-run file counts before prompting for action.
Do celebrate successful cleanups with cheerful mascot animations and exact freed megabytes, scaled to the actual amount freed (confetti tier: modest / solid / major).
Do provide 1-click rollback access for system tweaks and Windows Update policies.
Do use Lucide icons consistently across all UI elements.
Do render an ErrorBanner in every view that calls the native bridge, on every catch block -- never rely on the activity log alone.
donts: Don't use generic dark-mode neon glows that contradict the cheerful daylight aesthetic.
Don't hide consequences of destructive actions; always display affected path trees.
Don't run the GUI with elevated root or administrator privileges.
Don't pair gray text with colored background containers.
Don't let a failed action fail silently. addLog() alone is not user-facing feedback -- the terminal drawer defaults to closed.
